explainer_content.short_definition: The heavy riff road where blues-rock power becomes hard rock, arena crunch, and proto-metal weight.
explainer_content.history_capsule: Led Zeppelin, Black Sabbath, AC/DC, Deep Purple, and related bands made guitar repetition, volume, and rhythm-section impact the main event. Some records still swing like blues; others point unmistakably toward metal's darker mass.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It gave rock its durable heavy grammar: the riff as hook, the amplifier as identity, and the band as a physical force.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: The song usually starts in the guitar body, not the lyric. Melody matters, but the riff tells you where you are.
what_to_listen_for: A repeated guitar figure carrying the whole song
Bass and drums locked to the riff
Vocals riding over volume rather than smoothing it
